findings.evidence: Lines 152–160 read the ref SHA and later issue an unconditional DELETE. COORDINATION.md:87 says any expired lease is free for takeover via CAS, so takeover remains possible after the grace cutoff.
findings.fix: Delete through a compare-and-swap operation tied to the observed `sha`, such as `git push --force-with-lease=<ref>:<sha> origin :<ref>`, and treat a lease changed since observation as live; add a takeover-between-read-and-delete test.
findings.issue: Lease deletion is unconditional: after the sweeper reads an expired ref, a worker can CAS-update it to a live commit before the REST DELETE, which then deletes the worker's new lease. The one-hour grace only delays this race and does not prevent it.

summary: The sweeper can race a legitimate takeover and delete a newly live lease, so the central coordination guarantee is unsound.
